lines.japanese: グレタガルドに夜が来た。
lines.english: Night had fallen over Gretagard.

lines.japanese: フェニックスの副官が舵を握る自動四輪車は、電気の力でほの白く照らされた車道を、ユニコーンの早駆けにも劣らぬ速度で驀進していた。
lines.english: Phoenix’s lieutenant held the wheel as the self-propelled four-wheeled carriage raced down an electrically lit road, as fast as any galloping unicorn.

lines.japanese: 私は後部座席の窓にもたれ、革のシートに抱かれてまどろんでいた。ひとりで後部席を占拠しているレイヴンも同じようだ、ときおり不快そうに寝姿勢を変える以外は動かない。
lines.english: I leaned against the rear window and dozed in the embrace of a leather seat. Raven had a back seat to himself and seemed to be sleeping too. Apart from an occasional irritable shift, he did not move.

lines.japanese: 会話のない車内を満たすのは、あたかも地下隧道の逃走劇を思わせる冷ややかで攻撃的な音楽。乗り心地は不気味なぐらい快適で、城一番の御者に引かせる幌馬車でさえ比較にならないほどだ。
lines.english: Cold, aggressive music filled the wordless cabin, music fit for a desperate flight through an underground tunnel. The ride was unnervingly smooth. Not even a covered coach drawn by the finest driver in the castle could compare.

lines.japanese: 薄目を開けて窓の外を眺めていると、輝く色彩が水飴のように溶けて流れてゆく。
lines.english: Through half-lidded eyes I watched the brilliant colors outside melt and stream like ribbons of syrup.

lines.japanese: 「俺の知らぬ間に、夜はこんなにも明るく華やいだものになっていたのか」
lines.english: “Had night truly grown so bright and festive while I knew nothing of it?”

lines.japanese: 鈍重なまばたきを繰りかえしながら私はつぶやいた。
lines.english: I murmured, blinking heavily again and again.

lines.japanese: 「だからいまのグレタガルドには、闇を好む異形のものがいなくなってしまったのだな……」
lines.english: “So this is why the Gretagard of today has lost the misshapen creatures that delight in darkness...”

lines.japanese: 眠りに落ちているはずのレイヴンが、感心するように鼻を鳴らして寝返りを打った。
lines.english: Raven, who ought to have been asleep, gave an appreciative snort and rolled over.

lines.japanese: 「着いたよ」
lines.english: "We're here."

lines.japanese: 家々がせせこましく身を寄せあっている只中で、フェニックスは自動車を停めさせた。
lines.english: Phoenix had the automobile stopped amid a tight huddle of houses.

lines.japanese: 彼に促され、私は車中から硬い路面へ降りた。明るいだけで温かみのない街灯の光を浴びて、三角屋根の木造建築が立ちふさがっている。
lines.english: At his urging I stepped down onto the hard road. A wooden house with a peaked roof stood before me in the bright, cold light of a streetlamp.

lines.japanese: 「ほほん、ファルコンらの目を通して覚えはあったやもしれぬが……これが現在の余の居城であったか」
lines.english: “Ho-ho. I may have known it through Falcon's eyes, or another's... So this is my present castle.”

lines.japanese: わずか地上２階の家屋はひどく年老いて見えた。周囲のどの家よりも疲れきっている。働き盛りをとうに過ぎた木こりの翁のようだ。
lines.english: The house rose a mere two stories above the earth and looked terribly old. It seemed wearier than every building around it, like an aged woodcutter long past his working prime.

lines.japanese: 「いや、不平は申すまい。たしかに一国のあるじとして屈辱を覚えぬと言えば嘘になるが、しかし我は賢者王、いたずらに現実を拒絶するほど愚昧ではない」
lines.english: “No. I shall not complain. To claim I feel no humiliation as sovereign of a nation would be a lie. Yet I am the Sage King, not such a fool as to reject reality merely because it displeases me.”

lines.japanese: 「いい心掛けだね。そうやってちょっとずつ、この狂った世界にチューニング合わせていけばいいと思うよ」
lines.english: “That's the spirit. Keep tuning yourself to this crazy world a little at a time.”

lines.japanese: 禿げたトチノキを見上げていた私の背後で、フェニックスが言った。彼は台形の窓枠に片腕を預けて微笑んでいる。後部席のレイヴンはまだ眠っているようだった。
lines.english: Phoenix spoke behind me as I gazed up at a horse-chestnut stripped bare. One arm rested on the trapezoidal window frame, and he was smiling. Raven still appeared to be asleep in the rear seat.

lines.japanese: 「迎合し過ぎていまの伽楼羅を失ってほしくはないけどさ。いくらなんでも今日みたいなペースで突っ走ってたら、あっちゅー間に警察か病院連れてかれちゃうからね。郷に入りては郷に従えっつーじゃん」
lines.english: “I don't want you fitting in so completely that we lose the Karura you are now. But if you keep tearing ahead at today's pace, the cops or a hospital will haul you away in no time. When in Rome, right?”

lines.japanese: 「うむ、よう分からぬが、大儀であったぞ友よ。こたびの度重なる心遣い、深く感謝する」
lines.english: “I can’t say I understand, but you’ve done well, my friend. You’ve shown me kindness after kindness today. I thank you deeply.”

lines.japanese: 私は左腕で力こぶを作り、その下に右手を（ぱちんと鳴らしながら）通してフェニックスへ差しだした。この親しみやすい握手は、グレタガルド王家に伝わる、篤い友愛の情を示す表現手段である。
lines.english: I flexed my left arm, swept my right hand beneath it with a crisp clap, and offered that hand to Phoenix. This genial handshake, handed down through the royal house of Gretagard, is a means of expressing the warmest bonds of friendship.

lines.japanese: だが彼は平民の出自ゆえ、王室典範に明るくなかった。私の仕草を柔軟体操か何かとしか思わなかったのだろう、向けられたてのひらを無視して煙草を一本抜きだした。
lines.english: But as a man of common birth, he was unfamiliar with royal protocol. He must have mistaken my gesture for some manner of calisthenics: he ignored the waiting palm and drew out a cigarette.

lines.japanese: 「やー、今日は面白かったねえ。なんかすんげー昔のころ思いだしちゃった。友達とか妹と芝生のうえ走りまわってたころ──あれはいつ頃だったかなあ、ねえ？」
lines.english: “Man, today was fun. Had me remembering way, way back—running all over the grass with my friends and my little sister. When was that again, huh?”

lines.japanese: 「そうか。よし、それなら俺もダヴと遊んでやろう。うふふ、俺が帰ってきたと知ったらあの子は喜ぶぞ。うふふ、可愛いダヴめ」
lines.english: “I see. Very well, then I shall play with Dove too. Heh heh. How delighted the child will be when she learns I have returned. Heh heh, my darling Dove.”

lines.japanese: プリンセス・ダヴ──先代国王の遺した幼くも愛らしい王女──の笑顔を思って、私の頬はホブゴブリンの腹の肉のようにたるんだ。うふふ。
lines.english: At the thought of Princess Dove—the young and lovely princess left by the late king—my cheeks went slack as the belly of a hobgoblin. Heh heh.

lines.japanese: 「かるらー」
lines.english: "Karura."

lines.japanese: 「ぬん？」
lines.english: "Nnh?"

lines.japanese: フェニックスは車内の天井にぶら下がっていた細い鏡を一度見上げ、また向きなおって微笑んだ。
lines.english: Phoenix glanced once at the narrow mirror suspended from the ceiling, then turned back to me with a smile.

lines.japanese: 「んじゃ行くわ。また遊ぼねー」
lines.english: “Well, I'm off. Let's hang out again sometime.”

lines.japanese: 「うむ、明日も国が平和であればな」
lines.english: “Indeed—provided the kingdom still knows peace tomorrow.”

lines.japanese: 私は最後に、後部ドアの閉ざされている窓を覗く。頬杖で顔の半分を隠したレイヴンが、目蓋をなかば開けてこちらを凝視していた。
lines.english: Before they left, I peered through the closed window of the rear door. Raven, half his face hidden behind the hand that propped his cheek, stared back through half-open lids.

lines.japanese: 「ふむん、起きておったのか。レイヴン、冷眼の殺戮者よ、うぬとも機あらばまた会いたいものよのう」
lines.english: “Hmm. So you were awake. Raven, cold-eyed killer, I’d like to see you again when the chance comes.”

lines.japanese: 彼はガラスの向こうで、どるんと肩を揺らした。口元に貼りつけていた半握りのこぶしが外れてみると、口の端が吊りあがってかすかに笑っていた。
lines.english: Beyond the glass, his shoulders gave a heavy lurch. The half-clenched fist plastered over his mouth slipped away, revealing one corner of his lips raised in the faintest smile.

lines.japanese: そうして彼らを乗せた鉄の馬は、脱肛気味の尻の穴から灰色の屁を吹きちらかして滑りだしていった。
lines.english: And off slid the iron horse with its passengers, blowing gray farts from its slightly prolapsed asshole.

lines.japanese: さて私は羽田城のみずぼらしい城門をくぐり（錆びた鉄柵が真冬の鶴のように物悲しく鳴きました）、ほんの三歩分の小さな前庭を渡って、土と埃の匂いがする玄関扉の前に立った。
lines.english: I, meanwhile, passed through the shabby gates of Haneda Castle—the rusted iron fence cried as mournfully as a crane in the heart of winter—crossed the tiny front garden in all of three strides, and stood before a door that smelled of earth and dust.

lines.japanese: 「誰ぞ。誰ぞある」
lines.english: “Who attends me? Is anyone there?”

lines.japanese: ドアを開け、板張りの廊下の奥──闇に包まれた空間へ呼びかける。
lines.english: I opened the door and called into the darkness at the end of the wood-floored hall.

lines.japanese: 「栄えある王の凱旋であるぞ。者ども、とく出迎えよ」
lines.english: “Your glorious king returns! Come forth, all of you, and receive him at once!”

lines.japanese: 王の声は夜のしじまに呑まれていった。
lines.english: The king's voice sank into the silence of the night.

lines.japanese: 私はしばし待った。ちょうど見知らぬ家の納戸へ迷いこんだ小童のように、好奇心と警戒心を秤にかけながら周囲を観察して退屈を凌いだ。
lines.english: For a time I waited. Like a little boy who had wandered into the storeroom of a stranger's house, I kept boredom at bay by studying my surroundings, weighing curiosity against caution.

lines.japanese: 腰を折って靴箱の中を覗いていると、不意に階段の先、二階の廊下から光が漏れた。私は頭を起こしてそちらを見上げた。階段の最上段から、幼い童女が首を伸ばしてこちらを窺っていた。
lines.english: I had bent at the waist to inspect the shoe cupboard when light suddenly spilled from the upstairs hall. I straightened and looked up. A little girl craned her neck over the top step and peered down at me.

lines.japanese: 「む？　どうした娘、この城の者か」
lines.english: “Hmm? What’s wrong, child? Do you live in this castle?”

lines.japanese: 私が明朗な声で尋ねると、童女は言葉を濁して曖昧に頷いた──頷いたと言うより、ただ首を縦に動かしたと言うべきか。
lines.english: At my cheerful question, the little girl mumbled vaguely and gave an uncertain nod—though rather than a nod, perhaps I should say that she merely moved her head up and down.
"Um... who are you?"

lines.japanese: 「ふむん、何を恐れておる。余は怪しい者ではない、もそっと近う寄れ」
lines.english: “Hrm. What is there to fear? I am no suspicious fellow. Come a little nearer.”

lines.japanese: 「う、うん」
lines.english: "O-okay."

lines.japanese: 私が招くと、娘は階段の片端に身を寄せ、両手で壁を触りながら一段一段注意深く下りてきた。
lines.english: At my invitation, the girl pressed close to one side of the staircase and descended one cautious step at a time, feeling along the wall with both hands.

lines.japanese: 「お、おかえりなさい」
lines.english: "W-welcome home."

lines.japanese: しかし階段の半ばで血相を変えると──
lines.english: But halfway down, she went pale—

lines.japanese: 「どしたのその服！？」
lines.english: "What happened to your clothes!?"

lines.japanese: ──残りの踏み段は急ぎ足で一息に消化した。
lines.english: —then made short work of the remaining steps in one breathless rush.

lines.japanese: 「す、すごい血！　なんで？　けが？　病院行った？」
lines.english: "Th-that's so much blood! Why? Are you hurt? Did you go to the hospital?"

lines.japanese: 赤黒く汚れた私の着衣を間近にして、娘はひどくうろたえた。その臆病で優しい瞳に古い記憶が重なった。
lines.english: The sight of my clothes, stained dark red with blood, threw the girl into a panic. Those frightened, gentle eyes stirred an old memory.

lines.japanese: そうだ、間違いない。この気高き子女の名は──
lines.english: Yes. There could be no mistake. The name of this noble maiden was—

lines.japanese: 「プリンセス・ダヴ！」
lines.english: "Princess Dove!"

lines.japanese: 懐かしい親族の手を取ると、彼女は天敵に出くわした野ウサギのように悄然と身をすくませた。
lines.english: When I took the hand of my long-missed kinswoman, she cowered like a wild hare confronted by its natural predator.

lines.japanese: 「おお失礼、現在の名は小鳩様でしたな。お久しゅうございます、これはこれは大きうなられて」
lines.english: “Ah, forgive me. In the present age you are Lady Kobato, are you not? It has been far too long. My, my, how you have grown.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　えっ？　だだ、だれ？　千歳さん？」
lines.english: "Huh? Wh-what? Who are you? Mr. Chitose?"

lines.japanese: 「おや、私がお分かりにならない？　はは、いや、ごもっともですな。考えてみれば最後に姫とお会いしたとき、御身はまだピーマンも召しあがれぬほど幼くていらっしゃった」
lines.english: “What, you do not recognize me? Ha ha—no, it is perfectly understandable. When last we met, Princess, you were still so young that you could not eat even your bell peppers.”

lines.japanese: 突っ張るように固まっていたダヴの腕から、怯えと戸惑いが抜けて力みが緩んだ。彼女は私の瞳を覗きこむように顔を近づけてきた。
lines.english: The arm that had gone rigid in my grasp loosened as fear and confusion ebbed out of Dove. She brought her face closer as though to search my eyes.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あの……もしかして、あの、二番目のかたですか？」
lines.english: “Um... could you perhaps be... the second one?”

lines.japanese: 「に、二番目！」
lines.english: "Th-the second!"

lines.japanese: 心ないダヴの言葉に、私は少なからず眉をひそめた。しかし露骨に不快を示したりはしなかった（なぜなら礼節を知らぬ子供の非は、当人ではなく教育を施さなかった大人にこそあるからです）。
lines.english: Dove's heartless words made me frown. I did not, however, parade my displeasure—for when a child is ignorant of courtesy, the fault lies not with the child but with the adults who failed to teach her.

lines.japanese: 「うぉふん！　姫、畏れながら讒言申しあげます。いかに先代国王の妹君と言えど、誇り高き我らに序列を付けるなど、グレタガルド王家のレディとして好ましからざる振る舞いですぞ」
lines.english: “Hrrumph! Princess, with all due respect, I must protest. Sister to the late king though you may be, to rank proud men such as ourselves is conduct unbecoming a lady of Gretagard's royal house.”

lines.japanese: 「挙句の果てには、に、に、二番目とな！？　おおお、お戯れを申されるな！　余は嫡男、余は長兄、余は第一王子！　我より上に兄弟はおらぬ！」
lines.english: “And of all things—to call me th-the second! Oh, cease your jests! I am the heir! I am the eldest brother! I am the first prince! No brother stands above me!”

lines.japanese: 「は、はい……ええ、と……ごめんなさい？」
lines.english: "Y-yes... um... I'm sorry?"

lines.japanese: 案の定ダヴは、己の非を非と認識していなかったようだ。謝罪ひとつ口にするのにも、まるで問題集の解答ページを覗くようにこわごわ私の顔色を窺ってきた。
lines.english: As I suspected, Dove had not recognized her offense as an offense at all. Even to offer a single apology, she watched my face as nervously as a pupil stealing a look at the answer key.

lines.japanese: 「結構です。誤ることは罪ではありません、誤りを謝らぬことが罪なのです。さてプリンセス・ダヴ、愚生の名はいまだ御身のご記憶にございますかな」
lines.english: “That will suffice. To err is no sin; the sin lies in refusing to apologize. Now then, Princess Dove, does the name of this humble servant yet linger in your memory?”

lines.japanese: 「え、えと、ええと……いー、いたみ……さん？」
lines.english: “Um, well... I-I... Mr. Itami?”

lines.japanese: 「さよう、私めのことはガルーダもしくは伊丹伽楼羅とお呼びください」
lines.english: “Just so. You may call me Garuda, or Karura Itami.”

lines.japanese: 「しかし光栄ですな、覚えておいでだったとは。いやはや、なにしろ最後に姫とお会いしたとき、あなたはまだ初等魔法も修めておられぬほど幼くていらっしゃった。どうです、そろそろ使い魔の召喚ぐらいは──」
lines.english: “But what an honor—to think you remembered me. Why, when last we met, Princess, you were still too young to have mastered even elementary magic. Can you summon a familiar yet, perhaps—”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あのっ」
lines.english: "U-um!"

lines.japanese: 魔術の習得状況について尋ねようとした私の言を遮り、ダヴは脇に垂らした腕を自分の体より後ろ──廊下の奥──へ向けて振り子のように揺らした。
lines.english: Cutting short my inquiry into her progress in the magical arts, Dove swung the arm hanging at her side like a pendulum, pointing behind herself into the depths of the hall.

lines.japanese: 「お、お久しぶりです、あの、あのいま、おふろ沸かすんでっ、えと……テレビ……そう、テレビの部屋で待っててくださいっ」
lines.english: “I-it’s been a long time. Um, I’ll get the bath ready, so... the television... yes, please wait in the TV room!”

lines.japanese: テレビとは絵や音を出力するマジックアイテムのような箱だ。現代人はこれを娯楽や慰安やクラスで仲間はずれにされぬ目的で観賞する。つまりダヴは、私に貴賓室でくつろげと言っているのだ。
lines.english: A television is a box, much like a magic item, that produces pictures and sound. Modern people watch it for amusement, consolation, and to avoid being excluded by their classmates. In other words, Dove was inviting me to repose in the chamber reserved for honored guests.

lines.japanese: 「おお、ありがたき幸せ。小鳩様のお心遣いに深く感謝いたします」
lines.english: “Oh, what gracious fortune. Lady Kobato, you have my profound gratitude for your consideration.”

lines.japanese: 私は心優しきリトルプリンセスに祝福あれと祈りながら膝を上げ、踵を彼女の立っている段に載せた。
lines.english: Praying that blessings might rain upon the kindhearted little princess, I raised one knee and planted my heel upon the step where she stood.

lines.japanese: 「うあ！？　くく、靴は脱いでください脱いでください」
lines.english: “Wah! Y-your shoes—please take off your shoes!”

lines.japanese: ダヴは慌てて両てのひらを突きだし、ぞえっぞえっと私の体を押しもどした。
lines.english: Dove threw out both palms and pushed me back, shove by little shove.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あの、あのっ、日本ではおうちに上がるとき靴を脱ぎます」
lines.english: “Um, um! In Japan, we take our shoes off before going inside a house.”

lines.japanese: 「なに、靴を？」
lines.english: "What? My shoes?"

lines.japanese: そういえば……あの憎むべき翼人たちは「歩く」という行為の必要性が薄かったせいで靴を履く文化がなかったが、どうやらその慣わしがいまに残っているようだ。
lines.english: Come to think of it... those detestable winged men had possessed no culture of footwear, their gift of flight having largely freed them from the need to walk. Evidently the custom had survived into the present day.

lines.japanese: まったく忌々しい風習だが、フェニックスの語ったゴーニィ・リテワという諺を思いだして従うことにした（ここだけの話、明日の大勝利のために今日小さな敗北を被るという戦略もあるのです）。
lines.english: It was a thoroughly infuriating custom, but I remembered Phoenix's proverb—*When in Roam...*—and elected to comply. Between ourselves, there is also a strategy by which one accepts a small defeat today in pursuit of a great victory tomorrow.

lines.japanese: 「あー、うぉふん、これは失敬。すぽんすぽん。小鳩様、やはり服も脱いだ方がよろしいか？」
lines.english: “Ah—ahem. My apologies. Off, off. Lady Kobato, should I remove my clothes as well?”

lines.japanese: 私は履いていた靴を勢いよく脱ぎちらしながら（行儀良く揃えたりしないのは忌々しい風習に対するせめてもの反抗心である）、腰をしぼっている革帯に手をかけた。
lines.english: I sent my shoes flying with vigorous kicks—my refusal to arrange them neatly was the least rebellion I could offer against this odious custom—and laid a hand upon the leather belt cinched around my waist.

lines.japanese: 「いいっ、いいです！　服は、服はいいんです！」
lines.english: “No! That’s fine! Keep your clothes on!”

lines.japanese: 「むはははん、ご遠慮召さるな。たしかにグレタガルドの男は、自己の名誉を重んじるあまり協調性に欠けるきらいがあります。しかし姫、あなたの命令は我が名誉より重く、さらには我が命より重いのです」
lines.english: “Mwahaha, you need not stand on ceremony. It is true that the men of Gretagard, placing such weight upon their personal honor, can sometimes lack a spirit of cooperation. But Princess, your command carries more weight than my honor, and indeed more than my very life.”

lines.japanese: 「う、うん分かった、分かったからズボンは上げてください、上げてください」
lines.english: “O-okay, I understand, so please pull your pants up. Pull them up!”

lines.japanese: 「さようか……ふうむ、我が忠義の証をお見せできず残念だ。どうも今日はホーリーランスの具合が悪くて困るのう。早く私も射精をしてみたいものだ。おいフェニックス、俺はまだ童貞と呼ばれているか。さて──」
lines.english: “Is that so...? Hrm. A pity I cannot show you proof of my devotion. My Holy Lance has been in poor condition today, much to my distress. I should like to ejaculate myself before long. Phoenix, am I still called a virgin? Now then—”

lines.japanese: 靴を脱いだ私は、改めて板張りの段に乗った。
lines.english: Having removed my shoes, I mounted the wooden step anew.

lines.japanese: 「──姫、この城の貴賓室はどちらでしたかな」
lines.english: “—Princess, in what direction might I find this castle's guest chamber?”

lines.japanese: しかしダヴは、まるで目の前を四つ足のアロワナでも通りすぎていったかのような表情で私を見詰めていた。
lines.english: But Dove only stared at me with the expression of someone who had just seen an arowana stroll past on four legs.
“Princess?”
“Huh…?”

lines.japanese: 「いかがなされた。どこぞに小鳩様の言葉を失わせるほどの驚愕すべき狂人でもおりましたか」
lines.english: “What is the matter? Has some lunatic so astonishing as to rob Lady Kobato of speech appeared nearby?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あは……あの、いえそんな、き、気にしないでください。その、ちょっと、驚いただけなんです。いたみさんは悪いひとではないと思います」
lines.english: “Ah, ha… no, nothing like that. P-please don't worry about it. I was only a little surprised. I don't think you're a bad person, Mr. Itami.”

lines.japanese: 「ふむん？」
lines.english: “Hrm?”

lines.japanese: ダヴはなぜか私に遠慮しながら、なりたなりたと慌ただしく両手を振って否定した。相手を立てることを決して忘れない、とても心おくゆかしい少女である。
lines.english: For some reason, Dove waved both hands in frantic denial while going out of her way to spare my feelings. A truly modest girl, never forgetting to show consideration for another.

lines.japanese: そんな彼女の硬い笑顔に見入っていると、私は徐々に穏やかで温かな気持ちになっていった。もしやこれこそ市井の民草が口にする、恋とやらいう感情なのだろうか。
lines.english: As I gazed upon her stiff smile, a mild and tender warmth gradually filled my heart. Could this be the emotion common folk call love?

lines.japanese: 「結婚を前提に性交してください」
lines.english: “Please have sexual intercourse with me on the understanding that we shall marry.”

lines.japanese: 私はすっかり恋とやらをした心地になって、果敢なアプローチを試みた（いつの世も女というものは、強引な男と予測もつかないとびきりのサプライズを求めているものです）。
lines.english: Now entirely persuaded that I had fallen in love, I attempted a bold approach. Women in every age desire an assertive man and a magnificent surprise they could never have foreseen.

lines.japanese: ダヴはピクシーにつままれたような顔で呆然と私を見詰めていた。おそらく感激のあまり言葉が出てこないのだろう。
lines.english: Dove stared at me in blank amazement, as though bewitched by a pixie. She was doubtless too overcome with joy to speak.

lines.japanese: 「沈黙は肯定と認識してよろしいですな？」
lines.english: “May I take your silence as assent?”

lines.japanese: 彼女は何度も首を左右に振った。あまりに高速で往復させるものだから、私は彼女の頭が磨耗してもげたりしないか心配だった（しかし同時に、デュラハンを妻に娶るという夢想が私の好奇心を刺激したのも事実だ）。
lines.english: She whipped her head from side to side again and again. She moved with such speed that I feared her head might wear away and fly off—though at the same time, I confess, the fantasy of taking a dullahan to wife stirred my curiosity.

lines.japanese: だがグレタガルドの諺にも『生煮えキメラは龍をも殺す』とあるように、このプロポーズはいささか時期尚早だった。つまり彼女はまだ心の準備が整っていなかったのだ（気高き乙女はいつでも恋に臆病なものです）。
lines.english: Yet as the Gretagard proverb tells us, “Even an undercooked chimera may slay a dragon,” and this proposal had evidently come a little too soon. She was simply not prepared. Noble maidens are ever timid in matters of love.

lines.japanese: 「さようか……ふん、またとない好機を逃しましたな。お気の毒！　もはや次にあなたが結婚の二文字と真摯に向かいあうとき、私はすでに円熟した家庭を築いていることでしょうよ、ばふん！」
lines.english: “I see… Hmph. You have let a matchless opportunity escape you. How unfortunate! By the next time you face the word marriage in earnest, I shall already have established a mature and flourishing household. Bah!”

lines.japanese: 「は、はい、すいません」
lines.english: “Y-yes. I'm sorry.”

lines.japanese: 話しているうち、私は臆病なダヴの将来が心配になってきた。石橋の上を『飛行』の呪文まで唱えて渡るような人生も結構だが、ひとはときとして先の見えない濃霧の中へ踏みだす勇気も必要になるのだ。
lines.english: As we spoke, I began to worry for timid Dove's future. A life spent casting a spell of flight before crossing even the sturdiest stone bridge may be all very well, but there are times when one must find the courage to step into a dense fog with no view of the road ahead.

lines.japanese: 「畏れながら小鳩様の今後のため、御助言申しあげておきましょう。逃した魚は大きい、今日できることを明日に延ばすな、そして！　機会が二度扉を叩くなどとは考えるなッ！」
lines.english: “With all respect, Lady Kobato, allow me to offer counsel for your future. The fish that escapes is always the largest. Never put off until tomorrow what may be done today. And above all—never imagine that opportunity will knock twice!”

lines.japanese: 「ひっ……ご、ごご、ごめんなさいっ」
lines.english: “Eek… I-I'm s-s-so sorry!”

lines.japanese: 「さては姫、あなたもやはり、童貞が子孫を残すことは不可能だとお思いか？」
lines.english: “Tell me, Princess: do you, too, believe that a virgin can never leave descendants?”

lines.japanese: 「わ、わわわ分かりません」
lines.english: “I-I-I don't know.”

lines.japanese: 「申しあげておきますが私は不能ではない、いささか趣向が一般的でないだけなのです」
lines.english: “I would have you know that I am not incapable. My tastes are merely somewhat outside the ordinary.”

lines.japanese: 「ぜんぜんぜんぜん分かりませんっ」
lines.english: “I don't understand any of this at all!”

lines.japanese: 「お疑いであれば、いまここで射精してご覧にいれますが」
lines.english: “Should you doubt me, I can ejaculate for you here and now.”

lines.japanese: 「私よい子なのでそうゆうのぜんぜん分かりませんっ！」
lines.english: “I'm a good girl, so I don't understand anything like that!”

lines.japanese: ダヴは悲鳴のような声をあげて首を振りながら、摺り足で後じさってゆく。
lines.english: Dove backed away in shuffling steps, shaking her head and crying out in something close to a scream.

lines.japanese: ふむん、なるほど。彼女は自分のことをいまだ子供だと認識していたのか。ゆえに夫になる男との年齢差を気にしていたわけだ。
lines.english: Hrm. I see. She still considered herself a child. That was why the difference in age between herself and a prospective husband troubled her.

lines.japanese: 「もはは、ご案じ召さるな姫。なあに、あなたはすでに立派なレディですぞ」
lines.english: “Mwahaha, have no fear, Princess. Why, you are already a splendid young lady.”

lines.japanese: 私は慰めの言葉を口にした。ダヴはよほど照れたのか、困ったように顔を引きつらせて微笑んだ。
lines.english: I offered these words of consolation. So profound was Dove's embarrassment that her face tightened into a pained smile.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あの、えと……テ、テレビの部屋こっちですっ」
lines.english: “Um, well… th-the television room is this way!”

lines.japanese: それから逃げるように背を向けて歩きだした。そんなに恥ずかしがることはなかろうに。
lines.english: Then she turned and hurried off as if fleeing. There was no need for such bashfulness.

lines.japanese: 「まあまあ、お待ちなさい」
lines.english: “Now, now. Do wait.”

lines.japanese: 私は彼女の後ろから手を伸ばして捕えた。
lines.english: I reached out from behind and caught her.

lines.japanese: 「おや、図らずもこんなところにレディの兆候が」
lines.english: “Why, here is another sign of the lady, found quite by accident.”

lines.japanese: 「ほうほう、順調に膨らんでおいでだ。ふむん、良き手ごたえ。お喜びなさい、これは将来立派な乳房に育ちますぞ」
lines.english: “Indeed, they are swelling splendidly. Hrm, most promising in the hand. Rejoice, Princess: these will grow into magnificent breasts one day.”

lines.japanese: 「な、ななななな何を……」
lines.english: “Wh-wh-wh-what are you…”

lines.japanese: 「やや！？　姫、どうなされた、顔色がすぐれませんぞ」
lines.english: “What!? Princess, what ails you? Your complexion is poor!”

lines.japanese: 「は、はう、はうう……」
lines.english: “H-hah… haaah…”

lines.japanese: 「姫、姫、お気をたしかに！」
lines.english: “Princess! Princess, collect yourself!”

lines.japanese: 「う、ううっ……えううっ……」
lines.english: “U-uh… nnnh…”
“Princess!?”

lines.japanese: 「う、う、う」
lines.english: “U-uh—uh—”

lines.japanese: 「うあああああああん！」
lines.english: “Waaaaaaaaah!”
“Princesssss!?”

lines.japanese: ダヴは乱暴に私を振りほどいて駆けだした。難しい年頃である。
lines.english: Dove tore herself roughly from my grasp and fled. Hers is a difficult age.
